text:
Nikita Kucherov keeps scoring, and the rest of hockey keeps talking about his future. Trade columns have the Wild and the Mammoth as possible suitors, TSN's headline quotes Andrei Vasilevskiy: "Hope that something will change," and The Athletic's headline has Vasilevskiy hoping the two sides find a "perfect golden middle." Kucherov's answer on Wednesday was a hat trick in an 8-3 win in Buffalo.

Separate the noise from the team and Tampa Bay looks like a contender. The Lightning are 12-4-2 with 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), 55% at five on five, and they draw more penalties (4.5 a game) than they take (3.6). Their finishing is a little hot, about 6.6 goals above their chances, but not by a worrying margin. Ryan McDonagh and Erik Cernak have been outstanding, 14-5 with 61% of the chances, and the checking line of Zemgus Girgensons, Pontus Holmberg and Ilya Mikheyev has outscored opponents 10-4.

The worry is Brayden Point, on injured reserve. His line with Kucherov and Jake Guentzel was 8-2 with 59% of the chances, and prospect Sam O'Reilly is getting his chance in the gap; he picked up his first NHL point Wednesday. Charle-Edouard D'Astous has 10 points in his last 10, well ahead of his chances.

Our numbers give Tampa Bay a 94% chance at the playoffs, projecting about 106 points. The standings are not the question here. Kucherov's future is.
